whyNotReceipted: Diagnostic isolation, not a control measurement. It certifies no stop of any control; it identifies a defect IN THE INSTRUMENT. Receipting it would put an instrument diagnosis into the control evidence chain. Same measured-and-not-receipted pattern as F4B/experience-profile/bithire-editorial.DIVERGENCE.json.
phase: H-3 phase (1) -- isolate the residual cause
question: F4B-7 measured 54/11/54 painted rows where the static arm moved and the DB arm did not, while BOTH arms moved --ds-type-scale from 1 to 0.94. Which link breaks?
finding: THE DB ARM READINGS LAG EXACTLY ONE PHASE for DEPENDENT computed properties. Run 2, the probe own measure path, full 14-fixture roster: at the MUTATION phase (scale 0.94) the card still reports the BASELINE 15px / 13.125px; at the REMOVAL phase (scale back to 1) it reports the MUTATION values 14.1px / 11.5972px. The custom property itself is always current. The static arm is in phase, because each of its phases is a fresh page load with no pending recalculation to miss.
thereforeF4B7WasMisdiagnosed: The F4B-7 divergence is an INSTRUMENT ARTIFACT, not a cascade defect. DB_ARM_SCOPE_SHADOWING as I named it does not exist: the H-3 design already measured that four closed controls declare their channel in the same artifact scope and closed clean, and run 1 here shows the inline write propagates perfectly on the real bundle -- with no flush at all, the card moves 15px -> 14.1px and the title 13.125px -> 11.5972px, exactly the values the static arm produced.
alreadyDocumentedInTheTree: runtime/measure/index.mjs, inside readAll, carries a comment describing this exact failure mode: writing a custom property on the document element and calling getComputedStyle in the next CDP round trip returns the STALE value on a document of this size -- the descendant reads the property back at the new value while the dependent property still reports its pre-dial value. The existing offsetHeight flush, plus a two-rAF settle, is NOT sufficient at full roster size (14 fixtures).
openQuestion: BLAST RADIUS, unassessed. If the inline arm can lag, earlier DB-arm readings of DEPENDENT properties may be affected too. Those controls closed with ingressEquivalence holding, which a systematic one-phase lag would not allow, so the trigger is not universal. What decides it is a re-measurement, not an argument.
